articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 Turbo with Native Multimodal Reasoning Across Text, Image, Audio, and Video
articles.summary: OpenAI released GPT-5 Turbo, featuring deeply integrated multimodal reasoning that can jointly process text, images, audio, and video in a single inference pass rather than relying on separate encoder pipelines. The model demonstrates significant gains on complex scientific reasoning benchmarks and real-time video understanding tasks. This represents a shift from modality-bolted-on architectures toward truly unified foundation models.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves State-of-the-Art on Mathematical Olympiad Problems
articles.summary: DeepMind announced Gemini Ultra 2 scored a verified 92% on a curated set of International Mathematical Olympiad problems, surpassing all prior AI systems and most human competitors. The system combines advanced chain-of-thought reasoning with a novel formal verification step that checks proof validity before outputting solutions. The result reignites debate about whether current scaling approaches are sufficient to reach AGI-level reasoning.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Begins Limited Deployment in Automotive Manufacturing Lines
articles.summary: Tesla has started deploying its third-generation Optimus humanoid robots in select Gigafactory production lines for parts sorting, quality inspection, and light assembly tasks. The Gen 3 units feature improved dexterous manipulation with 22 degrees of freedom per hand and on-device vision-language models for real-time task adaptation. Tesla reports the robots are operating at roughly 60% the throughput of human workers but improving weekly through over-the-air policy updates.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics and Hyundai Unveil Atlas Commercial Platform for Construction and Logistics
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics officially launched the commercial Atlas platform, backed by Hyundai's manufacturing scale, targeting construction site logistics and warehouse operations. The electric humanoid robot features a completely redesigned actuator system delivering 40% more torque density than previous prototypes and can carry payloads up to 55 kg across uneven terrain. Early pilot customers include DHL and Skanska, with initial deployments planned for Q1 2027.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Constitutional AI 2.0 Framework with Verifiable Safety Guarantees
articles.summary: Anthropic published a technical paper and open-source toolkit for Constitutional AI 2.0, which introduces formally verifiable safety constraints that can be mathematically proven to hold under specified input distributions. The framework uses a combination of abstract interpretation and runtime monitoring to provide certificates of behavioral bounds. The release is seen as a significant step toward satisfying emerging EU and US regulatory requirements for high-risk AI deployments.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Risk Production of 1.4nm Gate-All-Around Process Node
articles.summary: TSMC announced it has commenced risk production on its A14 (1.4nm-class) process node using next-generation gate-all-around nanosheet transistors, roughly six months ahead of its original public timeline. The node promises a 25% performance improvement or 35% power reduction over N2, critical for next-generation AI accelerator chips. Major customers including Apple, NVIDIA, and AMD are expected to tape out designs in early 2027.

articles.title: Microsoft and Quantinuum Demonstrate Fault-Tolerant Logical Qubit Operations Below Error Correction Threshold
articles.summary: Microsoft and Quantinuum jointly demonstrated sustained fault-tolerant operations on logical qubits with error rates below 10^-6 per logical gate cycle, crossing a key threshold needed for practical quantum algorithms. The achievement was realized on Quantinuum's H3 trapped-ion system using Microsoft's new topological error correction codes. Researchers say this brings useful quantum advantage for certain chemistry and optimization problems within a 3-5 year horizon.

articles.title: Figure AI Raises $1.5B Series C to Scale Humanoid Robot Production for Commercial Warehousing
articles.summary: Figure AI closed a $1.5 billion Series C round at an $18 billion valuation, led by Microsoft and joined by NVIDIA and Bezos Expeditions, to scale production of its Figure 03 humanoid robot for warehouse and logistics customers. The company claims its robots can now autonomously learn new pick-and-place tasks in under 15 minutes using a foundation world model trained on millions of hours of manipulation data. Figure plans to have over 1,000 units deployed across customer sites by mid-2027.
